title: Shape a signal
description: Amplify a sample and cap its level at 60. The last expression of the block supplies the result.
exercise: Change the sample from 14 to 25. Predict which branch returns 60, then run it.

title: Read an inferred type
description: Use one identity function at bool and i32. Inspect its inferred signature and the concrete result of main.
exercise: Switch to Run to get 9. Replace keep(9) with keep(true) and compare the types of the two branches.

title: Handle a missing reading
description: A sensor supplies Some(18) or None. The success arm of if let binds the reading and the other arm supplies a fallback.
exercise: Replace Some(18) with None. Run it, then inspect the AST to see how the pattern conditional is represented.

title: Move a cursor
description: An inout parameter gives a function exclusive access to a mutable cursor. The caller can read its new column after the call.
exercise: Add a second advance(inout cursor) statement. Predict the final column. Then remove mut from the declaration and check the diagnostic.

title: Follow an allocation
description: Borrow a boxed sample for one observation, then move the allocation to its final consumer. Both reads contribute to the result.
exercise: Reverse the operands of the addition and replace first with observe(sample). Check what happens when the read follows the move.

title: Repair a type error
description: An integer channel count and a boolean flag reach the same addition. Ask the checker which operand needs to change.
exercise: Replace enabled in the addition with (if enabled { 1 } else { 0 }). Check the edit and run it to obtain 3.
expected: right operand of '+' expects i32, found bool

title: Trace a native branch
description: Generate C for a signed comparison. Find the conditional in the generated function, then follow its result into the C entry point.
exercise: Change the input from 8 to -8. Compare the interpreter result and the emitted C literal.

title: Classify GPU lanes
description: Classify signed inputs into three bands. The map profile uses one independent input and result per active GPU lane.
exercise: Evaluate -1, 0, 7 and 8. Inspect Rill IR to find both signed comparisons, then compare the CUDA and Vulkan LLVM entry points.
